script: 401k With A Side Of Revenge . When our first child was born, my ex forced me to quit my job. I had no savings, no daycare, no family to lean on. He said, "You're a mom now, you're done with that." I felt like I'd lost the world in a single breath. I couldn't even think about the future. The second kid was only two when I found out about his affair. He was verbally, emotionally, and sometimes physically abusive. When he hit our firstborn, I put him out in 2012. I thought that was it, that I'd finally had my space. I thought I was safe. I couldn't afford daycare, so I had to stay home. He wouldn't give me a dime, bragging "The courts haven't ordered me to give you a dime!" He lied to the bank, had my accounts frozen, then assaulted me when I filed for default in the divorce. He thought he'd cornered me, but that was just the start. He thought he had me cornered. The judge finally ordered him to pay child and spousal support six months after I kicked him out. It was $2,562 a month. He refused until garnishment hit, and by then he was $6k behind. I used that to get permission to move away. But here's the thing—moving meant more than a new address. A year after the divorce, I remarried. I checked the court docs and saw a box that said spousal support stopped upon remarriage if checked. It wasn't checked, so I figured I was good. Instead of filing for his retirement, I just took that year of spousal support—$12k—and left it alone. I thought I was winning. In 2017, he filed for sole custody out of nowhere. He'd found out I remarried and that I'd been getting spousal support the first year of my marriage. I told him I'd taken that money instead of filing for my share of his retirement. He demanded repayment. The judge ordered me to repay, increased child support, and deducted the repayment from that. I got an extra $20 a month and he repaid himself.
